lines.trans: Let me look at you properly, Javier! You grew taller than the piano!
I cannot believe you are staying in the exact same guesthouse, Madam Carmen.
Wait—so we rode the same train on Monday, and you took her suitcase?
By complete accident! At my cousin's flat I opened it and saw sheet music and a red ribbon.
Why did you leave my bag on the step at night and run away?
Because when I walked here on Monday evening, I saw my older brother walking down this street!

words.gloss: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)

lines.trans: Your older brother lives here in Valencia?
Yes. I panicked, rang your bell, and slipped the Friday note onto the handle.
Wait—and Wednesday night you checked in here under your real name?
I needed a quiet place nearby before Friday, and honestly forgot you still had my bag!
Until you called us on Tuesday asking us not to open the white parcel!
Everything in that white paper belongs to my brother Tomas, not me.

Because when I walked here on Monday evening, I saw my older brother walking down this street!

lines.trans: Your older brother lives here in Valencia?
Yes. I panicked, rang your bell, and slipped the Friday note onto the handle.
Wait—and Wednesday night you checked in here under your real name?
I needed a quiet place nearby before Friday, and honestly forgot you still had my bag!
Until you called us on Tuesday asking us not to open the white parcel!
Everything in that white paper belongs to my brother Tomas, not me.

Why did you leave my bag on the step at night and run away?

words.gloss: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)

lines.trans: Your older brother lives here in Valencia?
Yes. I panicked, rang your bell, and slipped the Friday note onto the handle.
Wait—and Wednesday night you checked in here under your real name?
I needed a quiet place nearby before Friday, and honestly forgot you still had my bag!
Until you called us on Tuesday asking us not to open the white parcel!
Everything in that white paper belongs to my brother Tomas, not me.
See you later!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle abierto.

examples.text: Abro la ventana por la mañana.
examples.trans: I open the window in the morning.

examples.text: Ayer abrimos la tienda temprano.
examples.trans: Yesterday we opened the shop early.

meanings.note: Por accidente means 'by accident'.

examples.text: El accidente está aquí.
examples.trans: The accident is here.

examples.text: Vemos los accidentes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the accidents from the door.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Used reflexively (alojarse) for staying at a hotel or inn.

examples.text: Muchos viajeros se alojan aquí.
examples.trans: Many travellers stay here.

examples.text: Nos alojamos en una casa tranquila.
examples.trans: We stayed at a quiet inn.

meanings.note: Alto y claro means 'loud and clear'.

examples.text: Es una pieza alta.
examples.trans: It is a tall piece.

examples.text: Alto y claro. ¿Estás junto a la fuentecita de piedra?
examples.trans: Loud and clear. Are you beside the little stone fountain?

meanings.note: Antes de means 'before' a noun or infinitive.

examples.text: Llegué diez minutos antes.
examples.trans: I arrived ten minutes early.

examples.text: Antes de salir, cierra la ventana.
examples.trans: Before leaving, close the window.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave.
examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Feminine noun taking el in the singular (el asa de la maleta / la taza).

examples.text: El asa de la maleta es de cuero.
examples.trans: The suitcase handle is made of leather.

examples.text: Sujeta la cesta por las dos asas.
examples.trans: Hold the basket by both handles.

meanings.note: Accented aún is interchangeable with todavía.

examples.text: El café aún está caliente.
examples.trans: The coffee is still hot.

examples.text: Aún no han abierto la puerta.
examples.trans: They have not opened the door yet.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.text: Todo va muy bien hoy.
examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.

examples.text: El té sale bien caliente.
examples.trans: The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Quedarse blanco means 'to go pale'.

examples.text: Es una pieza blanca.
examples.trans: It is a white piece.

examples.text: Mira, hay un sobre blanco doblado en el asa.
examples.trans: Look, there is a folded white envelope on the handle.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.text: La calle está aquí.
examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Camino veinte minutos hasta el centro.
examples.trans: I walk twenty minutes to the city centre.

examples.text: Caminamos despacio por el puente.
examples.trans: We walk slowly across the bridge.

meanings.note: Cerca de + noun = near something; de cerca = up close.

examples.text: Mi familia vive muy cerca.
examples.trans: My family lives very nearby.

examples.text: Mira esta página de cerca.
examples.trans: Look closely at this page.

meanings.note: Silk ribbon or adhesive tape.

examples.text: La cinta está aquí.
examples.trans: The ribbon is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cintas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ribbons from the door.

coger.gloss: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)

meanings.en: to take; to pick up; to catch (Spain)
meanings.note: Standard everyday Peninsula Spanish verb for picking up objects or taking transport (g -> j before o: cojo).

examples.text: Cojo el autobús cada mañana.
examples.trans: I take the bus every morning.

examples.text: Coge una taza limpia del estante.
examples.trans: Take a clean cup from the shelf.

colgar.gloss: to hang; to hang up (the phone)

meanings.en: to hang; to hang up (the phone)
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: cuelgo) and g -> gu in preterite 1st sg (colgué).

examples.text: Cuelgo el abrigo detrás de la puerta.
examples.trans: I hang my coat behind the door.

examples.text: Colgó los farolillos entre las ramas.
examples.trans: He hung the lanterns among the branches.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Entrar/salir corriendo = to run in / run out.

examples.text: Corro para no perder el tren.
examples.trans: I run so I do not miss the train.

examples.text: Los niños corrieron hacia la fuente.
examples.trans: The children ran toward the fountain.

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg crezco.

examples.text: El limonero crece fuerte al sol.
examples.trans: The lemon tree grows strong in the sun.

examples.text: Has crecido mucho estos tres años.
examples.trans: You have grown a lot these three years.

meanings.note: Preterite 3rd sg/pl spells y: creyó, creyeron.

examples.text: Creo que el tren llega a tiempo.
examples.trans: I think the train is arriving on time.

examples.text: No podía creer tanta buena suerte.
examples.trans: He could not believe such good luck.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.

examples.text: Déjame ayudarte con esa caja.
examples.trans: Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Desde entonces = since then.

examples.text: ¿Entonces nos vemos mañana a las ocho?
examples.trans: So shall we see each other tomorrow at eight?

examples.text: Desde entonces trabaja con nosotros.
examples.trans: Since then she works with us.

entrar.gloss: to come in; to go in; to enter

meanings.en: to come in; to go in; to enter
meanings.note: Pairs with en in Spain (entrar en la posada).

examples.text: Entra mucha luz por el balcón.
examples.trans: Plenty of light comes in through the balcony.

examples.text: Entramos en la tienda para resguardarnos.
examples.trans: We stepped into the shop to shelter.

meanings.note: Single step of a staircase (plural: escalones).

examples.text: El escalón está aquí.
examples.trans: The step is here.

examples.text: Vemos los escalones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the steps from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.text: Espere un momento, por favor.
examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.

examples.text: Esperamos que descanse muy bien.
examples.trans: We hope you rest very well.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.text: Este patio es muy tranquilo.
examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

examples.text: Esta mañana hace mucho sol.
examples.trans: This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Hermano mayor = older brother; hermano pequeño = younger brother.

examples.text: El hermano está aquí.
examples.trans: The brother is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hermanos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the brothers from the door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

llamar.gloss: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)

meanings.en: to call; to ring; to be named (llamarse)
meanings.note: ¿Cómo se llama? asks someone's name.

examples.text: Soy de aquí, mucho gusto.
examples.trans: I am from here, pleased to meet you.

examples.text: Alguien llamó por teléfono ayer.
examples.trans: Someone called by phone yesterday.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! is Spain's most common everyday farewell.

examples.text: Cruza el puente y luego gira.
examples.trans: Cross the bridge and then turn.

examples.text: ¡Hasta luego, que tengas buen día!
examples.trans: See you later, have a good day!

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el lunes, los lunes.

examples.text: El lunes está aquí.
examples.trans: The Monday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lunes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Mondays from the door.

meanings.note: Hacer la maleta = to pack one's suitcase.

examples.text: Esta maleta azul pesa mucho.
examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en la maleta.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in the suitcase.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el martes, los martes.

examples.text: El martes está aquí.
examples.trans: The Tuesday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los martes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Tuesdays from the door.

meanings.note: Hermano mayor = older brother; plural mayores.

examples.text: Es una pieza mayor.
examples.trans: It is an older piece.

examples.text: Conoces bien a los hermanos mayores, Mateo.
examples.trans: You know older brothers well, Mateo.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.text: ¿Me pasas la sal, por favor?
examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?

examples.text: Vivo aquí y trabajo aquí.
examples.trans: I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.text: Mi maleta es azul marino.
examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Tener miedo = be afraid; entrarle miedo = to panic.

examples.text: El miedo es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The fear is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el miedo.
examples.trans: We talk about the fear.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Agrees with the noun it describes.
In ahora mismo, meaning right now, mismo strengthens the time word ahora. Now comes from ahora; mismo supplies emphasis without agreeing with a person in this expression.

examples.text: Tenemos el mismo trabajo.
examples.trans: We have the same job.

examples.text: Ahora mismo estoy ocupada.
examples.trans: I am busy right now.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el miércoles, los miércoles.

examples.text: El miércoles está aquí.
examples.trans: The Wednesday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los miércoles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Wednesdays from the door.

meanings.note: De momento = for now.

examples.text: El momento está aquí.
examples.trans: The moment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los momentos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the moments from the door.

meanings.note: Accented más means 'more / most'; de más = extra.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco más de té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little more tea?

examples.text: Es la habitación más tranquila.
examples.trans: It is the quietest room.

meanings.note: Accented pronoun after para, por, a, de, sin (distinct from possessive mi).

examples.text: Esta taza de té es para mí.
examples.trans: This cup of tea is for me.

examples.text: Déjemelo a mí, por favor.
examples.trans: Leave it to me, please.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Necesito un bolígrafo para firmar.
examples.trans: I need a pen to sign.

examples.text: ¿Necesitan ustedes alguna toalla más?
examples.trans: Do you all need another towel?

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: ¡Buenas noches! = Good evening / Good night; esta noche = tonight.

examples.text: La noche está aquí.
examples.trans: The night is here.

examples.text: Vemos las noches desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the nights from the door.

meanings.note: Nombre y apellidos = full name.

examples.text: El nombre está aquí.
examples.trans: The name is here.

examples.text: Vemos los nombres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the names from the door.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos mañana por la mañana!
examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!

examples.text: Nos alegra mucho la noticia.
examples.trans: The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Covers jotted notes, musical notes, and review scores.

examples.text: La nota está aquí.
examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos las notas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Used directly (olvidé la llave) or pronominally with de (me olvidé de...).

examples.text: Nunca olvido una cara amable.
examples.trans: I never forget a friendly face.

examples.text: Olvidé mi paraguas junto al mostrador.
examples.trans: I left my umbrella beside the counter.

meanings.note: Plural los papeles.

examples.text: El papel está aquí.
examples.trans: The paper is here.

examples.text: Vemos los papeles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the papers from the door.

meanings.note: Wrapped package or parcel.

examples.text: El paquete está aquí.
examples.trans: The parcel is here.

examples.text: Vemos los paquetes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the parcels from the door.

meanings.note: Printed music sheets for piano or voice.

examples.text: La partitura está aquí.
examples.trans: The sheet music is here.

examples.text: Vemos las partituras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sheet music from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> i: pido, pidió).

examples.text: Pido un café con leche, por favor.
examples.trans: I will order a coffee with milk, please.

examples.text: El cartero me pidió una firma.
examples.trans: The postman asked me for a signature.

meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg pertenezco.

examples.text: Esta maleta pertenece a la vecina.
examples.trans: This suitcase belongs to the neighbour.

examples.text: Esos libros pertenecen a la biblioteca.
examples.trans: Those books belong to the library.

meanings.note: Tocar el piano = to play the piano.

examples.text: El piano está aquí.
examples.trans: The piano is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pianos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pianos from the door.

meanings.note: In Spain, un piso primarily means an apartment.

examples.text: El piso está aquí.
examples.trans: The flat / apartment is here.

examples.text: Vemos los pisos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the flat / apartments from the door.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.text: ¿Puedo ver la etiqueta otra vez?
examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: One word without accent (distinct from ¿por qué? = why?).

examples.text: Abro la ventana porque hace calor.
examples.trans: I open the window because it is warm.

examples.text: Sonríe porque huele a canela.
examples.trans: She smiles because it smells of cinnamon.

meanings.note: Charming small inn with rooms around a courtyard.

examples.text: La posada está aquí.
examples.trans: The inn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las posadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the inns from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine: la prima.

examples.text: El primo está aquí.
examples.trans: The cousin is here.

examples.text: Vemos los primos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cousins from the door.

meanings.note: Pura suerte = pure luck.

examples.text: Es una pieza pura.
examples.trans: It is a pure piece.

examples.text: Por puro accidente
examples.trans: By complete accident

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Plural reales.

examples.text: Es una pieza real.
examples.trans: It is a real piece.

examples.text: Espera: ¿y el miércoles por la noche te registraste aquí con tu nombre real?
examples.trans: Wait—and Wednesday night you checked in here under your real name?

meanings.note: Registrarse en un hotel = to check in.

examples.text: Nos registramos en recepción al llegar.
examples.trans: We check in at reception upon arriving.

examples.text: El huésped se registró con su pasaporte.
examples.trans: The guest checked in with his passport.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.text: Es una pieza roja.
examples.trans: It is a red piece.

examples.text: ¡Dígales que la mía tiene una cinta roja en el bolsillo de arriba!
examples.trans: Tell them mine has a red ribbon in the top pocket!

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Salgo temprano hacia la estación.
examples.trans: I leave early for the station.

se.gloss: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one

meanings.en: himself / herself / yourself / themselves; impersonal one
meanings.note: Reflexive, reciprocal, passive/impersonal pronoun, and indirect object le/les before lo/la.

examples.text: La puerta se abre despacio.
examples.trans: The door opens slowly.

examples.text: Aquí se oye el canto de los pájaros.
examples.trans: Here you can hear the birds singing.

meanings.note: Polite form of address: señora Carmen.

examples.text: La señora está aquí.
examples.trans: The madam is here.

examples.text: Vemos las señoras desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the madams from the door.

meanings.note: Everyday Peninsula favourite for 'place' or 'seat'.

examples.text: El sitio está aquí.
examples.trans: The place is here.

examples.text: Vemos los sitios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the place from the door.

su.gloss: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)

meanings.en: his; her; its; their; your (polite usted/ustedes)
meanings.note: Plural sus (su maleta / sus maletas).

examples.text: Aquí tiene su llave, señora.
examples.trans: Here is your key, madam.

examples.text: Sus habitaciones están en la primera planta.
examples.trans: Your rooms are on the first floor.

meanings.note: Accented sí means 'yes' (distinct from unaccented si = 'if').

examples.text: Sí, la habitación está lista.
examples.trans: Yes, the room is ready.

examples.text: ¡Claro que sí, pase usted!
examples.trans: Of course, come right in!

meanings.note: Por la tarde = in the afternoon; ¡Buenas tardes! = Good afternoon!; llegar tarde = arrive late.

examples.text: ¡Buenas tardes! ¿Tienen una habitación libre?
examples.trans: Good afternoon! Do you have a room free?

examples.text: Perdón por llegar un poco tarde.
examples.trans: Sorry for arriving a little late.

meanings.note: Object/reflexive pronoun corresponding to tú.

examples.text: Te guardo un rollo de canela.
examples.trans: I am saving a cinnamon roll for you.

examples.text: ¿Cómo te llamas?
examples.trans: What is your name?

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.text: Tenemos ocho habitaciones tranquilas.
examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Tocar el timbre = ring the bell.

examples.text: El timbre está aquí.
examples.trans: The bell is here.

examples.text: Vemos los timbres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bells from the door.

tocar.gloss: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)

meanings.en: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: toqué.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: Someone just rang the bell.

examples.text: De niño tocaba el piano los viernes.
examples.trans: As a boy he played the piano on Fridays.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Said alone to reassure someone ('Easy, don't worry!').

examples.text: Es una pieza tranquila.
examples.trans: It is a quiet piece.

examples.text: Seca, calentita y tranquila. Ahora decidme qué falta.
examples.trans: Dry, warm, and quiet. Now tell me what is missing.

meanings.note: Plural los trenes.

examples.text: El tren está aquí.
examples.trans: The train is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trenes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the trains from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented possessive (tu llave / tus llaves), distinct from accented pronoun tú.

examples.text: ¿Dónde está tu caja de herramientas?
examples.trans: Where is your toolbox?

examples.text: Reconocí tu letra enseguida.
examples.trans: I recognized your handwriting right away.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person singular verbs (¿quiere usted...?).

examples.text: ¿Cómo se llama usted?
examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: Pase usted por aquí, por favor.
examples.trans: Come this way, please.

venir.gloss: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)

meanings.en: to come (el verano que viene = next summer)
meanings.note: Irregular: vengo, vienes, viene, vine.

examples.text: Gracias por venir esta mañana.
examples.trans: Thank you for coming this morning.

examples.text: Nos vemos la semana que viene.
examples.trans: See you next week.

meanings.note: Irregular: veo, vi, visto.

examples.text: Desde aquí veo el puente de piedra.
examples.trans: From here I see the stone bridge.

examples.text: ¡Nos vemos luego en el patio!
examples.trans: See you later in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Siempre viajo en tren junto a la ventana.
examples.trans: I always travel by train next to the window.

examples.text: Viajamos a Valencia el lunes por la mañana.
examples.trans: We travelled to Valencia on Monday morning.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el viernes ('on Friday'), los viernes ('on Fridays').

examples.text: El viernes está aquí.
examples.trans: The Friday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viernes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Fridays from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb.

examples.text: Vivo a dos calles de la plaza.
examples.trans: I live two streets from the square.

examples.text: Mis primos vivieron aquí muchos años.
examples.trans: My cousins lived here for many years.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.
